# The Severed Lands — World Overview

## What Is This World?

The Severed Lands is a fractured realm — a pocket reality cut off from its origin by the Rift, a cascading dimensional wound that tears through the sky and the earth and everything in between. No one knows what lies beyond the Rift. No one knows if there IS a beyond. What is known: people fall through from other worlds. Sometimes they remember where they came from. Usually they don't.

The Rift doesn't simply destroy. It scatters. It transforms. A wolf exposed to a Rift surge becomes a riftwolf — violet-tinged, faster, meaner, wrong. A person exposed for too long becomes Hollowed — still alive, still thinking, but seeing things no one else can see, speaking in fragments of languages that don't exist. The Rift is not a portal. It's a wound. And it's been bleeding for centuries.

Geography bends where the Rift has touched it. Forests grow with trees that have no roots, suspended in midair. Rivers flow uphill in stretches where the Rift's energy lingers. Settlements cluster around stable zones — places where reality hasn't thinned. These are called Anchor Points, and they're the closest thing the Severed Lands has to safe ground.

## The Rift

The Rift appeared centuries ago — a tear in reality itself, violet-black and crackling, alive in a way that geology shouldn't be. It has been spreading ever since. Energy leaks from it constantly. Where that energy pools, creatures mutate. Where it surges, reality tears. Where it concentrates, Rift pools form — liquid violet light that hums at a frequency just below hearing.

The Rift's origin is unknown. Every culture in the Severed Lands has a theory: a failed god, a magical catastrophe, a punishment from whatever lies beyond. None are confirmed. None can be. The Rift doesn't answer questions. It just is — and it's getting worse.

What IS known: the Rift connects to other worlds. People emerge from it — disoriented, often amnesiac, always changed. These arrivals are called Riftborn. Some remember fragments of their home worlds. Most don't. All of them share one thing: they can't go back. Not yet. Maybe not ever.

## The Anchor Doors

Scattered across the Severed Lands are massive stone archways — the Anchor Doors. They predate human memory. They were built by a civilization called the Wardens, who left behind inscriptions, artifacts, and the Doors themselves. No one knows what the Wardens looked like or where they went. What remains is their work.

Seven Anchor Doors were known to exist. Four are confirmed destroyed or permanently dark. Two are unaccounted for — their locations lost to time and Rift surges. One — the Door beneath a settlement called Waystation — is dormant but intact. If it can be reactivated, it might provide a way through the Rift. It might provide a way home.

The Doors are dying. One by one, they're going dark. No one fully understands why, but the timing coincides with the Rift's expansion. The Doors stabilize reality around them — when a Door goes dark, the Rift rushes in. The land around dead Doors becomes Rift-touched within weeks. Within months, it's uninhabitable.

## The Riftborn

Anyone who arrives through the Rift is Riftborn. They come from different worlds, different eras, different realities. Some arrive with skills and memories intact. Most arrive with nothing — no name, no language, no understanding of what happened to them. The first thing every Riftborn learns is that the Severed Lands does not welcome them.

The settled population — the people who were born here, who've lived here for generations — views Riftborn with suspicion. They're associated with the Rift's dangers. Their arrival often coincides with Rift surges. Some settlements bar Riftborn entirely. Others tolerate them but never trust them. No settlement celebrates them.

This is the central tension of the Severed Lands: a world full of refugees who can't go home, living among people who see them as dangerous outsiders. Some Riftborn accept this and try to build new lives. Others can't let go. They want to find a Door. They want to go back.

## The Returners

The Returners are a network of Riftborn who've banded together around a single goal: reactivate an Anchor Door and return to their home worlds. They're led by V — the oldest known Riftborn, a figure who arrived decades ago and retained memories of their original world. V has spent years studying the Anchor Doors, mapping Rift behavior, and gathering others who want to return.

The Returners aren't an army. They're refugees with a purpose. Their headquarters is Waystation, built around the dormant Door. From there, they send out patrols to scavenge Warden artifacts, map Rift surges, and search for the two unaccounted-for Doors. They share knowledge. They protect each other. And they're running out of time — with every Door that goes dark, the window for return narrows.

Internally, the Returners are divided. Some have given up on going home and want to build lives in the Severed Lands. Others are radical — willing to force a Door open regardless of consequence, regardless of what might come through first. V holds the faction together through sheer force of will and decades of accumulated trust, but the cracks are widening.

## Thornwall and the Settled

Thornwall is the largest human settlement — a merchant town built within the walls of an ancient fortress, ruled by a council of trading families. It's stable, prosperous, and deeply suspicious of Riftborn. The council maintains order, protects trade routes, and keeps Riftborn at arm's length. Some council members advocate for outright expulsion.

Thornwall represents the settled perspective: the Severed Lands is their home. They didn't fall through the Rift — they were born here. Riftborn are associated with danger, with surges, with instability. The council's official position is tolerance with caution. The unofficial position is less generous.

But Thornwall is not monolithic. One council family has been quietly funding Anchor Door research — they have their own reasons to want the Doors functional. And the town's underbelly is full of Riftborn who've learned to pass, to hide, to survive. The tension between Thornwall's public face and its private reality is one of the setting's driving conflicts.

## The Hollowed

Not all Rift-touched are beasts. The Hollowed are people — human, Riftborn, it doesn't matter — who've absorbed too much Rift energy. It changes them. They see things others can't. They speak in fragments. Some are harmless: prophets, oracles, drifters who mutter truths they shouldn't know. Others are dangerous — they've learned to channel Rift energy, weaponizing the very thing that broke them.

The Hollowed believe the Rift is not a wound but a transformation. They revere it. Some actively seek deeper exposure, pushing themselves closer to the Veil — the boundary between reality and the Rift. The deeper they go, the more powerful and less human they become.

The Hollowed have no formal leader, but whispers name someone called "the Warden" — a figure who may be the oldest Hollowed, or something else entirely. Their goal, if they have one, is unknown. Their unpredictability makes them impossible to negotiate with and dangerous to ignore.

## The Wardens

The Wardens were the civilization that built the Anchor Doors. They're gone now — extinct or hidden, no one knows which. What they left behind: the Doors themselves, fragments of their language, a handful of functional artifacts, and a recurring symbol — a circle bisected by a straight line — found at every Door site and on every Warden relic.

Warden artifacts are the most valuable objects in the Severed Lands. They're the key to understanding the Doors, and possibly the key to reactivating them. They're also fragmentary — most surviving artifacts are broken pieces of larger wholes. Collecting all fragments of a Warden artifact unlocks its full power. This is one of the Returners' primary activities: scavenging Door sites, trading for fragments, piecing together the Wardens' legacy one shard at a time.

## Riftbeasts

Normal animals exposed to Rift energy transform. The process is progressive: the more energy a creature absorbs, the more powerful and less recognizable it becomes. A wolf becomes a riftwolf — violet-tinged, faster, pack-hunting with an intelligence that normal wolves don't have. A bear becomes a riftbear — nearly unkillable by conventional means, regenerating near Rift pools. The transformation is permanent and irreversible.

Riftbeasts are not summoned. They're not from another world. They're what happens when the Rift touches something that was already here. Advanced riftbeasts develop the ability to phase-step — short-range teleportation through the Veil. The oldest and largest, the Elder Riftbeasts, are unique named encounters with territories, legends, and custom abilities. Each one is a boss fight waiting to happen.

Riftbeast territory defines the map of the Severed Lands. The Cairnfields are their heartland — an expanse of stone pillars and unstable ground where Anchor Door fragments litter the landscape. The Verdant Margin is their hunting ground — a forest where Rift-accelerated growth means trees that grow overnight and prey that's always abundant. Wherever Rift pools form, riftbeasts follow.

## The Premise

The Severed Lands is a world of refugees and ruins, of ancient technology and bleeding reality. The Rift is spreading. The Doors are dying. Someone — or something — is sabotaging efforts to reactivate them. And somewhere out there, V is tracking a lead that might change everything.

A campaign set here follows a simple arc: arrive through the Rift, survive the first encounter, find the Returners, piece together what the Wardens left behind, discover who's been working against the Doors, and choose — go home, or stay.

The world is designed to make both choices feel earned. Home is a real possibility, if the Door can be opened. But the Severed Lands is also a place worth staying for — full of people who've built lives from nothing, a world that's beautiful despite its wounds, and the kind of purpose that only comes from fighting for something that might not survive.
